name: What kitchen layout works best when the room is narrow?

mainEntity.name: What kitchen layout works best when the room is narrow?

acceptedAnswer.text: A compact kitchen can work well when each zone has a clear purpose and doors do not compete for the same space. Use appliance dimensions, cabinet depths, corner conditions, and traffic from adjacent rooms to test whether an L-shaped, galley, or single-wall plan is most efficient. An island may consume more room than it adds if it reduces preparation or circulation space. Tape the layout at full scale and simulate opening appliances and cabinets. Elite Remodeling & Design can compare layout options using the existing space and your intended use.
acceptedAnswer.description: Galley, single-wall, or compact L-shaped layouts often work better than forcing in an island, but the best choice depends on doorways, windows, appliance sizes, and traffic. Tape each option at full scale and test open doors, cabinet access, and meal preparation.
